topology.cycle_note: The only cycle in the property is Living room to Hall and back, through archways A and B. Every other room hangs off the Hall by a single edge, and a single edge cannot contradict itself. That one cycle is the property's only means of catching its own stitching error.
topology.archway_note: Every Hall connection is an open archway. At the photo tier this is the best possible case: an archway carries a through-view, so every adjacency in the property has direct image evidence and none has to be guessed. A property behind closed doors would leave most edges structurally invisible at this tier.
topology.benchmark_gap: The flip side is that the benchmark now contains no closed-door adjacency at all, so the photo tier's worst failure mode goes unmeasured. Staging one - close the Living room's wall D door, or hang a sheet over an archway, and re-capture - would cost one extra capture and turn an unmeasured weakness into a reported interval.
topology.unassigned_note: Three Hall openings have no named destination and three bedrooms have no named opening. The pairing is near-certain but is not stated, and adjacency is scored.

open_questions: Where does the Living room's archway_b (0.855 m, on its wall B) actually lead? The Hall has no opening of that size. This decides whether the property has a loop at all.
Which way does the Hall's wall C step go - does segment C2 push outward or cut a bay inward? 1.92 m2, an 11% swing on Hall floor area, and the polygon cannot close without it.
Are the balcony and parking space inside the stitched floor plan, or excluded as exterior?

layout_from_sketch.note: Wall A's four archways map onto the four rooms in the east column, in order. That is what confirms arch_a3 and arch_a4 as the two eastern bedrooms rather than leaving them unassigned.

discrepancy_living_room_archway_b.what: The Living room records two archways: archway_a at 2.013 m, and archway_b at 0.855 m, both said to lead to the Hall. The Hall's wall C carries only two openings - the 2.013 m Living room archway and a 0.787 m archway to bathroom_2. There is no 0.855 m opening anywhere on the Hall.

archway_b is the Hall's arch_a3 at 0.875 m - but that is on wall A, on the opposite side of the Hall from the Living room, so this is geometrically implausible.

discrepancy_living_room_archway_b.why_it_matters: This is the property's only cycle. If archway_b does not reach the Hall, the room graph is a pure tree, no placement can contradict another, and the loop-closure residual the drift ablation depends on does not exist on this property.
